sources.entry: Quillite Markdown - Lightweight, local-first Markdown reader and editor with live preview, visual diagrams, math, and multi-format export.

summary.one_liner: Quillite Markdown (轻阅 Markdown) is a local-first, Go + Wails desktop Markdown reader and editor for Windows, macOS and Linux with live rendering, source and split preview, Mermaid/ECharts diagrams, and KaTeX formulas.
summary.what_it_does: The app is a desktop Markdown tool built with Go and Wails, explicitly not on Electron, with a Windows installer of about 13 MB according to the README. It has an "instant render" editing mode where formatted Markdown is edited in place, and a source mode with a split preview that can be swapped left or right. It supports 22 Mermaid and 19 ECharts diagram types with visual editors for common ones, and 95 formula templates rendered locally with KaTeX and mhchem. Documents can be exported to Word, HTML, PDF, PNG/JPEG and portable Markdown, with extra formats if Pandoc is installed. Other features include a table designer, image handling with local assets folder, optional PicGo image hosting integration, offline English spell checking, file recent/favorites lists, and conflict handling when a file changes outside the editor. Optional AI editing and checking use the user's own API key and require confirmation before sending content.
use_cases: maintain technical notes in a Markdown folder
create flowcharts, Gantt charts and other diagrams in Markdown
export Markdown to Word, PDF or HTML
notable: Instant-render editing that edits formatted Markdown in place, with a source mode and split preview
22 Mermaid and 19 ECharts diagram types with visual editors for common types
95 formula templates for math, physics and chemistry rendered locally via KaTeX/mhchem
Portable Markdown export that embeds local images into a copy without changing the original
Conflict handling that compares disk and editor versions instead of silently overwriting
caveats: Windows and macOS installers are not signed with a production certificate, so SmartScreen or Gatekeeper prompts may appear on first install
Instant-render mode is not full WYSIWYG for every Markdown extension; complex syntax falls back to source
PDF export prefers a local Edge/Chrome/Chromium, and extra export formats need Pandoc installed
Some features (AI, PicGo uploads, feedback, analytics) require network access and are opt-in or user-triggered
